clusters.name: Authentication Security Controls
clusters.description: Authentication controls vary by credential mechanism and validity enforcement, distinct from payment processing, data retention, workflow modeling, and reporting.

relations.rationale: Verified user identity is typically required before CityBike authorizes sensitive operations such as payment or bike rental actions.

clusters.name: Sensitive Data Retention Policy

saturation_history.rationale: All open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The payment-related codes fit the Payment Provider Integration Strategy dimension (facade delegation, multiple backends, strategy-based abstraction, interchangeable implementations). The biometric login and immediate deletion codes are covered by Authentication Security Controls and Sensitive Data Retention Policy, respectively. The verification-code expiry/TTL/timeout codes are all variants of the existing authentication validity-enforcement value. The report builder, downloadable report, and construction-vs-export separation codes are captured by Usage Report Construction and Delivery. The state-machine/user-journey, navigation, QR unlock, rental progression, and payment-state codes are covered by Rental Workflow State Modeling. No open code introduces a distinct architectural concern outside the current dimensions for the CityBike use case.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing dimensions. Rental duration tracking and pre-expiry notification handling map to Rental Workflow and Timing Control (dimension 4), especially the scheduler-based duration and pre-expiry notifications value. Observer-based bike status change notifications, usage history availability notifications, observer-based bike availability update, and real-time availability notification are covered by Real-Time Event Notification Pattern (dimension 8). Immediate session termination on logout and manual session invalidation supported fit Authentication and Session Controls (dimension 1). Identity and contact data collection, optional location attribute capture, and security-focused form handling are captured by Personal Data Governance and Retention (dimension 2), with the privacy/compliance aspect also compatible with Data Encryption Protection (dimension 6) for protected flows. Password-based authentication setup is not a new architectural concern in this taxonomy relative to the use case; it falls under authentication/session control rather than a separate dimension. Proximity-based bike lookup and location-aware query handling are already covered by Bike Location Tracking Strategy (dimension 7). The encryption-related codes are absorbed by Data Encryption Protection (dimension 6), which already spans transit, storage, registration, authentication, and payment flows. The state pattern for rental lifecycle is covered by Rental Workflow and Timing Control (dimension 4) as the lifecycle/state-machine axis. Scheduler-driven timing notifications are likewise covered by dimension 4. No genuinely new architectural dimension appears in this minibatch.
